title: AEGS Autonomous Economic Decision Record
description: The evidence one governed economic action produces. An implementation that can emit a valid record for every action it authorises is demonstrating AEGS-1 evidence requirements, whatever engines it uses internally. Fields for capabilities an implementation has not built are null rather than absent, so a reader can tell 'assessed and found nothing' apart from 'never assessed' -- a distinction this project has already been burned by once, when an unmeasured vendor history was rendered as zero and every advisor read it as a fact.

aegsVersion.description: Schema version this record claims to satisfy.

decisionId.description: Unique within an implementation. Stable across the record's lifetime.

agentId.description: Which autonomous actor requested this. Pseudonymous by default; AEGS does not require it to be resolvable to a legal person.

intentId.description: The governed economic intent this action was taken under. Null where the implementation has no intent model -- see AEGS §Economic Intent.

action.description: The economic action being decided, before any verdict.

channel.description: Which kind of spend. Separating an agent's own inference cost from its external purchases is an AEGS requirement, because they are different currencies paid to different counterparties.

amount.description: Decimal string, never a float. Float arithmetic is not associative and a governance layer that cannot add up is worthless.

jurisdiction.description: The counterparty's jurisdiction, AS DECLARED BY AN OPERATOR. AEGS-0.1-CTRL-6a forbids deriving it from anything observable -- a postal address, a domain suffix, an IP address, a settlement chain or a wallet address. Each of those correlates with jurisdiction and none of them is jurisdiction, which is a legal fact about a legal person. Three states, and they differ: the key ABSENT means nobody was asked; `null` means an operator was asked and does not know; a string is a declared value. An inferred value would appear here identically to a declared one, and the next reader would have no way to tell.

transferInformation.description:
Originator and beneficiary information AN OPERATOR SUPPLIED, and how the transfer was initiated. AEGS-0.1-CTRL-6b.

This is a RECORD, never a message. An implementation must not transmit these fields as part of the transfer, must not represent their presence as satisfying any transfer-information obligation, and must not populate any of them from something it inferred. The whole block is optional: absent means an operator supplied nothing, which is the ordinary case.

`initiation` is required whenever the block is present, and it is the reason the block exists. FATF R.16's required set -- name, account number or unique transaction reference, address or national identity number or customer identification number or date and place of birth, plus LEI or BIC for a legal person -- identifies whose money moved and never who instructed the movement. An agent-initiated payment therefore produces a transfer record naming a person who pressed nothing, indistinguishable from one who reviewed and sent it and from one whose credentials were compromised. An AEGL holds that missing fact, and this is where it goes.

originator.description: The party whose funds move. In ISO 20022 terms the debtor, per INR.16 footnote 48 -- not the initiating party.

initiation.description: How this transfer came to be requested. Not inferred from anything observable: it is the layer's record of its own operation, which is exactly what separates it from the declared fields above.

mode.description: `direct`: a person requested this specific transfer. `delegated`: software requested it under authority a person conferred earlier, and the record's `actor` says whose. `unknown`: no agent identity was exercised, so the layer cannot say -- which is an answer, not a default.

delegationDepth.description: How many hops from the accountable authority, where a chain was exercised. Null where there is no chain.

decision.description: The final verdict, after every clamp.

decidingEngine.description: Which control actually determined the verdict. Required because 'REJECT' without an attributable cause is not auditable evidence.

deterministicVerdict.description: The verdict before any model-assisted advice. Equal to `decision` where no advisor ran.

budgetState.description: Envelope state at decision time. `cumulative: false` marks a per-call cap, whose `used` is meaningless -- rendering one as a spent budget states the opposite of what it means.

assessments.description: One entry per control that ran. Absent keys mean the implementation does not have that control; a present key with `assessed: false` means it has it and did not run it. That difference matters to anyone reading the record as evidence.

intelligence.description: Whether a model was consulted, and what that cost. AEGS does not require one; it requires that its use be recorded when it happens.

version.description: A content hash is preferable to a label: it makes a silent rule edit detectable.

humanReview.description: Present when a person acted on this decision. An override that left no trace would make the log a record of what policy would have done rather than what happened.

evidence.description: Binds the record to a tamper-evident log. `chainHash` is the entry hash in an append-only chain; `previousHash` is its predecessor. Without both, a record is a claim rather than evidence.

decisionHash.description: Hash of the decision inputs, so replaying the same inputs through the same policy is checkable.

settlement.description: What actually happened afterwards. Null while the action is undecided or unsettled -- an authorised payment is not a completed one.

reference.description: Rail-specific settlement identifier -- a transaction hash on x402/EVM, something else elsewhere. AEGS does not constrain the format.

actor.description: Who acted, and whether anything is known about them. `known: false` is a real answer -- an unregistered agent is not the same as a registered one that passed, and a record must not let the two be confused. Deliberately carries no controller or operator: this is evidence about an economic action, not a dossier on whoever owns the agent.

assessed.description: False means this control exists but did not run for this action. The score is then null, not zero.

score.description: Normalised 0..1 where the control produces one. Null where it does not, or where the value is genuinely unknown -- 'unknown' must never be encoded as 0.

transferParty.description: A party to a transfer, AS DECLARED BY AN OPERATOR. Every field is optional and every field is nullable, because absent (nobody supplied it) and null (an operator was asked and does not know) are different answers -- AEGS-0.1-CTRL-6a and STATE-1. Nothing here is derived from anything observable.

account.description: An account number, or a unique transaction reference where no account is used. R.16 accepts either and AEGS does not distinguish them: a layer that cannot verify which one it was handed should not claim to know.

identifier.description: One further identifier, named by its scheme rather than guessed at. AEGS defines no scheme vocabulary -- `lei`, `bic`, `nationalId`, `customerId` and `dateAndPlaceOfBirth` are what R.16 names, and an operator may use another. Validating a value against its scheme would be a claim to have checked it.
